operator_decisions.title: Ethics self-assessment
operator_decisions.gate: phase_06_gate predicate g07_p06 requires a non-empty ethics_assessment.self_assessment_statement in the Phase 6 output.

decision.personal_data_gdpr: Yes, limited. The DrR web MVP holds user accounts and farm contact details; field boundaries tied to a named holding are personal data for a natural-person farmer. ELTE's Data Protection Officer reviews the processing and data minimisation applies.
decision.farmer_commercial_data: Yes. Yields, irrigation records and field geometries from AgroVIR farms are commercially sensitive. A data-sharing agreement governs them, and results are published only in aggregated or anonymised form.
decision.human_participants: Yes, low risk. Task T5.6 requires structured feedback from AgroVIR staff and participating farmers. Informed consent and a right of withdrawal apply. No health, biometric or special-category data is collected.
decision.animal_subjects: No. The project studies processing tomato.
decision.dual_use_and_misuse: No. Civil agricultural decision support on open Copernicus data. No export-controlled goods or technology.
decision.non_eu_data_transfer: No. All data stays within the EU (Hungary and Bulgaria).
decision.ethics_committee_approval_required: Not yet determined. ELTE's research ethics committee will be consulted on task T5.6 before any fieldwork begins. The expectation is that structured usability feedback collected under informed consent, with no special-category data, falls below the committee's review threshold. To be confirmed in writing by M12.
decision.data_protection_officer_consulted: Planned. ELTE's Data Protection Officer will be consulted before the first DrR Web MVP user account is created, covering the lawful basis for holding farm contact details and field boundaries, the retention period, and data minimisation across the MVP.

operator_decisions.consequence: ethics_issues_identified is true, so Part A's ethics self-assessment table and Part B-2 §6 must both be completed. Phase 6 writes the two amended lines above into the self-assessment statement rather than leaving them as bare tokens.
operator_decisions.source_ref: Operator input pack item 3, candidates accepted with the C2 amendment of 2026-08-11.

operator_decisions.title: Security screening and Green Charter statements
operator_decisions.gate: None. Part B-2 §7 and §8, which this run does not draft.

decision.security_screening: No concerns arise. The project handles no classified or EU-restricted information. It uses open Copernicus data and institutional field measurements. It involves no dual-use goods or technology and no entity established outside the EU.
green_charter: Reuse before regeneration: the five-year MATE archive is the primary data source rather than a new campaign.
Prefer the simplest adequate model, introducing deep architectures only where sample size and temporal density justify them.
Run computation on shared ELTE infrastructure rather than provisioning dedicated hardware.
Travel: default to remote collaboration, with at most one physical visit to MVCRI per growing season and shared transport for field campaigns.
Conferences: hybrid attendance by default, at most one in-person conference per year.
Purpose: the project targets better irrigation timing, which serves the Charter's environmental aim directly.

operator_decisions.note: The security statement's claim that no entity is established outside the EU is true of the consortium as it stands — ELTE and MATE in Hungary, MVCRI in Bulgaria, AgroVIR in Hungary — and is unaffected by the placement decision.
operator_decisions.source_ref: Operator input pack item 13, candidates accepted 2026-08-11.

decisions.reframed_from: The operator's first answer, 'developing further the MVP prototype', which he then reframed rather than replaced. An MSCA placement must serve the fellow's training and not the host company's engineering. The draft calls the MVP the research-to-operation demonstrator and not the primary scientific objective. And §2.2 records the DrR components as the fellow's background IP, so six months developing her own prototype inside a commercial partner raises an ownership question the proposal has not addressed.
